messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: KV-HEAP memory spike on hosted-runtime pool us-east-1. Multiple OOMs observed; error rate increased. Severity: P1.
Oncall_Maya: saw the alert. investigating now. starting with heap / k/v metrics.
Anjali: looking at tail logs — lots of sessions with extremely long prompts (200k+ tokens) causing continuous batching to hold huge KV windows.
Maya: confirming. continuous-batcher backlog jumped from 10->450 in <2m. Heap feed shows kv_heap_bytes per worker spiked to 96% of JVM heap.
Mike: any customer-facing errors?
Elaine: support queue: 3 customers reporting timeouts and 1 exec complaining about token errors in prod. potential impact to two enterprise tenants.
Jordan: dumping top keys to see large context owners. running: `curl -s http://metrics/kv/top-keys | head -n 50`
Anjali: output shows repeated session ids with huge prefix growth; looks like a prefix-amplification loop from a customer bot that re-sends prior transcript in full each turn.
Maya: plan: 1) throttle prefetch/prefix for hosted runtime pools. 2) reduce batch size to limit in-flight KV growth. 3) evict oversized sessions. need deploy approval for hotpatch.
Ops_lead: approve emergency hotpatch. go ahead with config change first (no restart).
Maya: applying runtime config: `continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens=4096 -> 1024` and `prefetch.max_prefix_tokens=8192 -> 2048`. Pushing to us-east-1 hosts via runtime-config-system.
deploy-bot: runtime-config update started: change-id cfg-2026-03-hotfix-1.
Maya: also triggering eviction for top 20 offending sessions to reclaim heap: `kv-ops evict --session $(cat top_sessions.txt)`
Jordan: eviction job kicked off, initial reclaim ~22% heap per worker. latency is dropping on the affected machines.
Anjali: logs show OOMs reduced after eviction; continuous-batcher queue now 40.
Maya: good. rolling the smaller-batch setting to remaining hosts in region. monitoring traces.
Mike: what's the residual customer impact? Elaine, can you confirm which customers were affected and whether requests were lost or retried?
Elaine: two enterprise customers saw 5xx for a window of ~3m. We have request IDs and will send a short comms. No data exfiltration.
Anjali: root cause hypothesis: prompt-echo bot + batching heuristic combined to keep very long KV windows alive; a regression in recent batching optimizer removed an earlier prefix-length cap.
Jordan: I pulled the change: PR 5487 relaxed prefix trimming in optimizer. rolling back that PR is safest next step.
Maya: next steps: 1) keep lowered batch/prefetch caps (deployed) 2) revert PR 5487 from canary and schedule runtime patch 3) add short-term auto-evict rule for sessions > 50k tokens 4) customer comms via support.
Ops_lead: assign action owners: Anjali -> PR revert + test; Jordan -> eviction safety checks + autop-run; Mike -> postmortem writeup; Elaine -> customer comms drafts.
Anjali: will open a revert PR in 10m and run unit+integration on staging. making sure we preserve perf for normal workloads.
Maya: monitoring: memory heatmap returning to normal, error rate dropping to baseline within 6m after full rollout. still watching for recurrences.
Elaine: drafting message: "We observed degraded performance caused by unusually long prompts from a third-party integration; we fixed routing and throttled excessive sessions and have mitigation in place. Support will follow up with affected tenants." will share for review. :memo:
Mike: reminder for postmortem: include the batching optimizer change and why it bypassed prefix cap, include test gaps.
Maya: oncall handing off to Jordan for overnight watch. Jordan, please escalate if it recurs.
Jordan: ack. I'll keep an eye on continuous-batcher metrics and set an alert for kv_heap delta > 10%/5m.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated — reduced to P2. Automated rollback planned for next maintenance window unless revert PR is merged.
Maya: thanks all. moving to postmortem channel when we finish notes. good job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:
